item.title: Bloc needs to ‘up its game’ on securing raw materials, auditors find
item.description: The three areas of improvement needed, according to the Luxembourg-based European Court of Auditors (ECA), are diversification of trade partners, more domestic production, and recycling, reusing and substituting.

item.title: Secrecy Tracker: Transparency battles shaping the EU in 2026
item.description: Dear readers, Welcome back to Secrecy Tracker, with our first update of the year on what the EU is keeping behind closed doors. I’m Alexander Fanta, a journalist with Follow the Money. In this edition, we focus on key transparency developments shaping 2026, offering a sneak preview of the legislative and legal changes likely to […]

item.title: Listen: Will the EU compromise on green policies to mine critical raw materials?
item.description: As Europe races for green tech, mining projects spark protests from Sweden to Portugal. With China's dependence looming, is the EU abandoning environmental caution to secure a critical raw materials supply? Does this mean we are observing a shift from a precautionary approach?

item.title: Punching below your weight – Europe needs to escalate North Korea sanctions
item.description: The EU decisionmakers have not updated the North Korea sanctions list in almost two years, even though the DPRK is fighting a war in Europe.

item.title: Europe’s friends, foes — and fantasies — in this Chinese Year of the Fire Horse
item.description: The new EU narrative on India reflects a modesty, pragmatism and flexibility that has long been absent from its dealings with the Global South. The unhelpful habit of dividing the world into democracies and autocracies is fading, replaced by a grudging acknowledgement that the EU is a middle-sized power which must work harder to find its place in a multipolar world, writes Shada Islam.

item.title: EU opens probe into Chinese wind giant Goldwind under foreign subsidies rules
item.description: This is the first high-profile case in the wind sector, although the EU Commission stressed the opening of a probe "does not prejudge the outcome of the investigation."

item.title: ‘Made in Europe’ talks expose Paris-Berlin fault line, ahead of EU competitiveness retreat
item.description: Ministers responsible for competitiveness met for two days in Cyprus, but the talks produced little in the way of concrete decisions, and suggest an agreement on “Buy in Europe” rules is still some way off.

item.title: German NGOs sue Elon Musk’s X again over election research data access
item.description: X (formerly Twitter) is being sued in Germany by NGOs over Digital Services Act obligations, for a second time. Researchers want access to platform data before the key Hungarian parliamentary election in April.

item.title: EU still wary of Trump on Greenland, as Russia pounds frozen Ukraine
item.description: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said she didn't know "what comes next" with US claims on Greenland, but Europe remained sure Russia was a long-term threat.

item.title: EU ‘caving into the floodgates of anti-migrant rhetoric’ warns Human Rights Watch
item.description: The EU's obsession with migration has radically shaped its foreign policy — while at home its laws are eroding away asylum, warns Human Rights Watch.
